anchor.intro: {TIMECHECK} Welcome to GLC News. Coming up: the White House launches a twenty-four seven Trump TV stream, the E.P.A. begins screening drinking water for abortion-pill traces, Google backs a nuclear uprate deal in Georgia, and new lawsuits over vision loss tied to popular weight-loss drugs.
anchor.outro: Thanks James for that report. That is our GLC News bulletin for now. Thank you for listening.

reporters.handoff: First, Edith on the White House stream and a new E.P.A. water study.

stories.topic: White House launches Trump TV 24/7 stream
stories.script: The White House has launched Trump TV, billed as The Essential Station, a twenty-four seven stream of administration videos, major presidential remarks, and highlights. Coverage from the Daily Mail and White House posts says the feed began Monday evening on WhiteHouse.gov and the official White House YouTube channel, promoted as continuously updated in real time. The rollout comes days after the administration barred several news networks from covering the White House, with officials framing the channel as a direct way to reach viewers outside traditional news outlets.

stories.topic: EPA drinking water study screens for abortion-pill traces
stories.script: The Environmental Protection Agency is launching a scientific drinking-water study that will screen samples from several metropolitan areas for more than one thousand four hundred emerging contaminants, including the abortion medications mifepristone and misoprostol. The Hill reports the work uses non-targeted analysis and can show whether a substance is present, not how much is there or whether it poses a health risk. E.P.A. says it is lining up water systems for a study expected to run over about the next year, with results published after quality review. The agency framed the project as research under the Safe Drinking Water Act, not a new nationwide monitoring rule.

reporters.signoff: I am Edith, for GLC News.

reporters.handoff: Thanks Edith. Isabella next, on Google and Georgia nuclear power.

stories.topic: Google funds nuclear uprates at Vogtle and Hatch
stories.script: Georgia Power and Google announced an agreement, pending Georgia Public Service Commission approval, for Google to support nuclear uprates at Plants Vogtle and Hatch. The upgrades are projected to add about ninety-six megawatts of capacity for Georgia Power customers, with Google's subscription expected to enable about nine hundred million dollars in customer benefits over the life of the units. Southern Company and Georgia Power filings describe a new Nuclear Uprate tariff and an extended power uprate request for Hatch, while Vogtle units one and two already had uprate approval in the twenty twenty-five integrated resource plan. The companies say the deal aims to add carbon-free power as data-center demand rises, without shifting upgrade costs onto non-participating customers.

reporters.signoff: I am Isabella, for GLC News.

reporters.handoff: Thanks Isabella. James now, on weight-loss drug lawsuits and vision loss.

stories.topic: Lawsuits allege Ozempic Wegovy Zepbound cause irreversible vision loss
stories.script: U.S.A. Today reports dozens of lawsuits allege popular obesity and diabetes drugs can cause irreversible vision loss. Patients say Ozempic and Wegovy from Novo Nordisk, and Zepbound and related G.L.P. one medicines from Eli Lilly, are linked to non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, a rare condition that can bring sudden permanent vision damage. Federal claims are consolidated in multidistrict litigation three one six three in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania, with roughly two hundred cases pending and early briefing on causation and warnings underway. Manufacturers dispute the claims, research remains mixed, and no verdicts or settlements have been reported.

reporters.signoff: I am James, for GLC News.
